props.gloss_en: R' Yonatan: 'you have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride, with one of your eyes' (Song 4:9) -- at first, with one of your eyes; when you do, with both your eyes
Ulla: insolent is the bride who is unfaithful under her own wedding canopy
Rav Mari: the verse [for Ulla's saying] is 'while the king was at his table, my spikenard gave forth [its fragrance]' (Song 1:12)
Rav: and still [His] affection is with us
Rav: for it is written 'gave forth [its fragrance]' and it is not written 'reeked'

the baraita: those who are insulted and do not insult, hear their shame and do not answer, act out of love and rejoice in sufferings -- of them the verse says 'and those who love Him are as the sun going forth in its might' (Judg 5:31)
R' Yochanan: 'the Lord gives the word; those who proclaim are a great host' (Ps 68:12) -- every utterance that went forth from the mouth of the Almighty divided into seventy languages

the school of R' Yishmael: 'and like a hammer that shatters rock' (Jer 23:29) -- as this hammer splits into many sparks, so every utterance that went forth from the mouth of the Holy One divided into seventy languages

Rav Chananel bar Pappa: 'hear, for I speak negidim' (Prov 8:6) -- why are words of Torah likened to a nagid? to tell you: as a nagid has power to put to death and to grant life, so words of Torah have power to put to death and to grant life
Rava: to those who go to the right with it [Torah] it is a drug of life; to those who go to the left with it, a drug of death
another reading: 'negidim' -- to every utterance that went forth from the mouth of the Holy One, two crowns are tied

R' Yehoshua ben Levi: 'my beloved is to me a bundle of myrrh that lies between my breasts' (Song 1:13) -- Knesset Yisrael said before the Holy One: Master of the world, though my beloved distresses and embitters me, he lies between my breasts
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: 'my beloved is to me a cluster of henna in the vineyards of Ein Gedi' (Song 1:14) -- He whose is everything atones for me for the sin of the kid that I gathered for myself
Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman: this karmei is a term of gathering [answering the stam's 'how is that implied?']
the mishna: a launderer's chair, on which they gather (koremim) the garments
